title: High Resolution 3D Imaging of the Human Pancreas Neuro-insular Network
protocol: Cut through the paraffin perpendicular to the surface of the tissue using a new razor blade or scalpel.
Loosen and remove the tissue from the paraffin using forceps or a spatula.
Scrape excess paraffin from the tissue gently with a spatula.
Incubate the tissue in xylene for 24 h at room temperature.
Transfer and incubate the tissue in fresh xylene for another 24 h at room temperature.
Transfer and incubate the tissue in 100% ethanol for 24 h at room temperature.
Transfer and incubate the tissue in 95% ethanol for 24 h at room temperature.
Transfer and incubate the tissue in 70% ethanol for 24 h at room temperature.
Rinse the tissue in 0.01 M phosphate buffered saline (PBS).
Place the tissue in 0.01 M PBS in a conical tube to equilibrate for 24 h at room temperature.
Pipette 10 mL of 16% PFA into a 50-mL conical tube.
Add 4 mL of 0.1 M PBS to the tube.
Add 26 mL of distilled deionized water (ddH2O) to the mixture.
Close the cap and mix briefly.
Dissect the pancreas sample into smaller pieces no more than 1 cm thick if larger than 1 x 1 x 2 cm.
Fix the pancreas sample in freshly prepared 4% PFA at 4 °C for 48 h.
Wash tissue sample in three changes of 0.01 M PBS for at least 15 min each wash.
Store the tissue in a 15 mL centrifuge tube in 0.01 % PFA/0.01 M PBS or 0.5 % sodium azide/0.01 M PBS until use.
Section the tissue into 1 - 2 mm thick sections for further processing using a vibratome to assist in even sectioning.
Place a flask on the ice in a bucket on top of a magnetic stir plate.
Add a magnetic stir bar to the flask.
Add 147.8 mL cold ddH2O (4 - 8 °C) to the flask.
Add 20 mL of 0.1 M PBS to the flask.
Add 20 mL of cold 40% acrylamide solution (4 - 8 °C) to the flask.
Add 12.2 mL of 16% PFA solution to the flask.
Add 250 mg VA-044 initiator to the flask.
Mix the hydrogel solution with a magnetic stir bar for at least 10 min.
Leave the solution on ice.
Place a 15-mL conical tube in the ice next to the flask containing the hydrogel solution.
Pipette 14 mL of monomer solution into the conical tube.
Add one piece of 1-2 mm thick fixed tissue sample to the tube.
Cap the tube with the tissue sample inside.
Incubate the sample in monomer solution for 3 days at 4 °C, protecting from light.
Aliquot any remaining monomer solution and store at -20 °C for future use.
Prepare a bucket of ice.
Place the sample-containing conical tube on ice.
Gather 2-3, 18-gauge hypodermic needles per sample.
Obtain paraffin film and a timer.
Connect tubing to the nitrogen tank.
Pierce the cap of the conical tube containing the sample with one side carefully.
Press one hypodermic needle through until it is under the surface of the liquid monomer solution.
Use another hypodermic needle to puncture the opposite side of the cap without submerging it.
Connect tubing from the nitrogen tank to the submerged hypodermic needle.
Slowly turn on the nitrogen until bubbling steadily through the liquid is observed.
Allow nitrogen to bubble through the liquid for 10 minutes.
Quickly remove both needles after bubbling stops.
Cover the cap with paraffin film immediately after removing needles.
Place degassed sample in an incubator at 37 °C for 3 hours.
Prepare 500 mL clearing solution (4 % SDS at pH 8.5) by adding 50 mL of 0.1 M PBS and 20 g SDS powder to ~300 mL ddH2O while stirring.
Adjust the pH using sodium hydroxide and hydrochloric acid to 8.5.
Add ddH2O until final volume reaches 500 mL for clearing solution.
Pour away excess hydrogel after polymerization and discard into chemical waste container.
Gently wipe away remaining hydrogel from sample with a paper towel and discard into chemical waste container.
Wash the sample in 3 - 5 exchanges of 0.01 M PBS, discarding wash fluid into chemical waste, for 15 minutes each step.
Transfer the sample to a 50-mL conical tube containing 40 mL clearing buffer.
Incubate the sample at 37 °C and change to fresh clearing buffer every other day.
Leave the sample in the clearing buffer for 2 - 8 weeks depending on the sample size.
Monitor tissue clearing and stop when complete.
Hold the sample up to the light to check for proper clearing.
Wash the samples on a shaker at 60 rpm at room temperature for one day with 40 mL of 0.01 M PBS, changing to fresh buffer often (4 - 5 buffer changes in total).
Let the final wash continue overnight at room temperature.
Prepare PACT staining buffer by adding 50 mg sodium azide and 0.5 mL TritonX-100 to 500 mL of 0.01 M PBS.
Mix well.
Incubate the sample with primary antibodies.
Add 2% normal serum (same species as the secondary antibody) to the base PACT staining buffer in a 2-mL flat bottom tube.
Add primary antibody to the 2% serum/PACT staining buffer in a ratio of approximately 5x the standard concentration.
Use a spatula to remove the sample from the wash buffer and dab excess buffer onto a paper towel.
Place the sample into the tube containing the primary antibody solution.
Incubate for 2-4 days at room temperature on a shaker at 60 rpm.
Wash samples thoroughly at room temperature on a shaker at 60 rpm using 0.01 M PBS, changing to fresh buffer 4-5 times and leaving the final wash overnight.
Add 2% normal serum (same species as the secondary antibody) to the base PACT staining buffer in a 2-mL flat-bottom tube for a total volume of 1 mL per sample/tube.
Dilute secondary antibodies at a concentration of 1:200 and add them to the buffer.
Remove the sample from the wash buffer using a spatula, dab excess buffer onto a paper towel.
Place the sample into the tube containing the secondary antibody solution.
Incubate for 2 days at room temperature on a shaker at 60 rpm while protecting the sample from light.
Wash the samples thoroughly in 0.01 M PBS on a shaker at room temperature and 60 rpm, changing buffers 4-5 times.
Leave the final wash buffer overnight while protecting from light during washing.
Prepare refractive index matched solution (RIMS) buffer by weighing out 11 g of non-ionic density gradient medium into a 50-mL conical tube.
Add ~5 mL of 0.02 M phosphate buffer to the powder and mix well with a spatula, releasing air from the powder as needed.
Bring the volume to 10 mL using additional phosphate buffer, mixing thoroughly.
Incubate RIMS at 37 °C until dissolved, inverting and gently mixing as necessary.
Transfer samples into RIMS by pipetting 1 mL of RIMs into a 2-mL flat-bottom tube.
Remove sample from wash buffer with a spatula, dabbing off excess buffer onto paper towel, then place in the tube with RIMS solution.
Gently tap the tube to submerge the sample in RIMS.
Place samples in RIMS on the bench protected from light at room temperature for 2-4 days before imaging.
Prepare an 8-well coverslip bottom chamber slide for imaging by adding just enough RIMs to coat the bottom.
Add the prepared sample to one of the wells and cap the slide for imaging.
Select appropriate lasers for the excitation and emission spectra of the fluorophores used.
Adjust settings of the acquisition software to eliminate overlap between channels.
Use separate tracks if necessary when two fluorophores have similar excitation spectra.
Choose maximum acquisition speed, 16 bit, 4 or more averages, and 1024 x 1024 resolution.
Zoom into the object to be imaged.
Set up the z-stack with optimal sectioning for the objective being used.
If deconvolution is desired later, use a z-step smaller than optimal such as 1 µm.
Begin nearest the surface of the tissue and increase gain as the objective focuses through the z-plane.
Add corrections while focusing without changing laser settings.
Acquire a test stack with one average and 512 x 512 resolution at maximum speed.
Check the image in 3D to ensure equal brightness throughout the stack for each color before acquiring the final high-resolution z-stack.
Ensure that samples have been equilibrated in RIMS for imaging for at least 24 hours.
Transfer samples to fresh RIMS in the imaging chamber and allow to equilibrate for at least a day.
Mount the sample for imaging.
Select the smallest capillary for mounting the sample.
Use putty or a dish to hold the sample while applying super glue to the end of the capillary.
Glue the tissue to the capillary touching as little surface of the tissue as possible.
Insert the sample for imaging.
Image using 5X or 25X objectives suitable for optically cleared samples with pivot scan option.
If shadowing or blurring occurs, rotate the sample and try again, or let the sample continue to equilibrate in RIMS.
